speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with a generalized rash; to help you, I will ask a few quick questions. Has the rash appeared since birth, or did it show up later?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) Infection.

The rash appearing only 1 day after birth in a term infant with no prenatal care is highly suspicious for a transplacental or early contact transmission of a herpes virus, rather than a neonatal gonococcal infection which typically presents with a more pustular or purulent discharge rather than a simple generalized rash. I have noted the maternal history of gonorrhea, but the timeline and presentation do not fit that diagnosis well. Given the severity, we must rule out HSV immediately. REQUEST TEST: PCR (CSF, Blood, and Swab of lesion). REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_photo_of_rash.
